geeklist.description:
[url=https://www.yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/352224][b]VFM Alphabetical List 1[/b][/url] | [url=http://bgg.activityclub.org/tools/vfm.html?listid=352224][b]VFM Alphabetical List 2[/b][/url] | [color=#969696]VFM Posting Tool[/color] | [thread=3452199][b]VFM Admin Thread[/b][/thread] | [geeklist=352231][b]VFM Wish List[/b][/geeklist]
[b]Thank-you for a successful VFM.[/b] Enjoy the rest of your convention. Looking forward to seeing everyone again in 2026.
Every VFM suffers from a handful of no-shows during the Exchange, most are resolved during the con. Please use your contact information, if the seller/buyer remains unresponsive [b][url=https://boardgamegeek.com/geekmail/compose?touser=StormbringerGrey]send me[/url][/b] the contact info.
[size=18][b]Sellers, one last task: Please Pay the BGG Commission.[/b][/size]
• Per BGG’s TOS, sellers are required to pay BGG 3% commission for the use of this list. • The BGG mark-as-sold button must be used. • Instructions for canceling sales if needed is in the [thread=3452199][b]admin thread.[/b][/thread] • In about a week I will send GeekMail to any sales that are not properly marked for commission. • In about a month I will send any sales that are still not properly marked to BGG admin.
[b]Please note:[/b] This GeekList will no longer be moderated except for the purpose of assisting with commission payments.

Hey Folks... Just an observation, [b]there are a lot of auctions posted with no mention of end conditions[/b]. The posting tool defaults to an auction so make sure that is what you really want, if it is, you are required to say something about when it will end... even if its "whenever I feel like ending it". It's only fair to bidders that they know something about how long they will be committed to your auction. All auctions must be concluded by 11:59PM July 1, 2025 or earlier.

Hi All, the Terms of Service (ToS) have been updated to provide more clarity on auctions. I am reposting the new section below. Note that many of the currently posted auctions are in violation of the first bullet point, I will begin issuing friendly but direct requests to correct starting next week. Please post on the [thread=3452199][b]VFM Admin[/b][/thread] thread if you have questions or comments.
[b]⚠️Notes Specific to Auctions:[/b] • All auctions must include an End Date (mandatory). If your auction includes an end time (optional but recommended), that end time must be expressed in EDT (the convention time zone). • All auctions must have an end date/time no later than midnight prior to the first full day of the convention. Auctions may end sooner. • The following auction elements are optional: [c] [/c]o A starting price (minimum bid) - optional but highly recommended. If not stated, the starting bid is assumed to be $0 [c] [/c]o A minimum dollar increment ($1 is assumed) [c] [/c]o A “Buy It Now” or [b]BIN[/b] is completely optional • Any bid that meets or exceeds the starting bid is binding on both the bidder and the seller. The current high bidder may not retract their bid, the seller may not withdraw an item with a binding bid. Remember that bids lower than the starting bid are not binding. • Sellers may not include items with binding bids as part of an unrelated bundle or math trade. Once a binding bid has been made an item has been sold by auction, the only remaining question is to whom and for how much.

[q="StormbringerGrey"] [c] [/c]o A starting price (minimum bid) - optional but highly recommended. If not stated, the starting bid is assumed to be $0 • Any bid that meets or exceeds the starting bid is binding on both the bidder and the seller. The current high bidder may not retract their bid, the seller may not withdraw an item with a binding bid. Remember that bids lower than the starting bid are not binding.[/q] These are conflicting statements. That means I could bid $0 a listing with a BIN but no SB and the seller would be obligated to sell it to me if no one outbids me.
I use the following rules for the VFM I run, which is possibly a bit clearer: [q]Please adhere to the naming conventions for the pricing format. If no pricing format has been specified, then the entry will be considered to be using the BIN with no SB option.
[b]Starting Bid or SB:[/b] You will not accept any price below this amount, but are committed to sell if anyone bids at or above this amount. Sellers, please make sure to make it clear when you will be closing the item to bids.
[b]Buy It Now or BIN:[/b] You will immediately accept the first offer at that amount. If a starting bid (SB) has not been specified, then the seller is open to lower offers, but is not required to sell below the BIN amount. Sellers, if you do not have an SB specified, please respond to bids below your BIN within a timely fashion.
[b]Fixed Price or FP:[/b] This is the only price you are willing to accept. Buyers should not bid any other amount. [/q]

OK, hopefully this removes the ambiguity while still remaining reasonably straighforward.
[b]⚠️Notes Specific to Auctions:[/b] • All auctions must include the following: [c] [/c]o End Date (mandatory). [c] [/c]o All auctions must have an end date/time no later than midnight prior to the first full day of the convention. Auctions may end sooner. [c] [/c]o A Starting Bid - this may be $0 but remember that any bid that meets or exceeds the starting bid obligates the seller to conclude the auction on the end date with the high bidder being the winner. Offers lower than the starting bid may be treated as low ball offers and are not binding on either party. • The following auction elements are optional: [c] [/c]o End time (optional but recommended). Note that if you include an end time, that time must be expressed in EDT (the convention time zone). [c] [/c]o Auctions may include anti-sniping variability in end conditions as long as the approach to anti-sniping is clearly stated. [c] [/c]o A minimum dollar increment ($1 is assumed) [c] [/c]o A “Buy It Now” or [b]BIN[/b] is completely optional. An item with a BIN but no starting bid and no end time is not an auction and is functionally the same as a fixed price offer. • Any bid that meets or exceeds the starting bid is binding on both the bidder and the seller. The current high bidder may not retract their bid, the seller may not withdraw an item with a binding bid. Remember that bids lower than the starting bid are not binding. • Sellers may not include items with binding bids as part of an unrelated bundle or math trade. Once a binding bid has been made an item has been sold by auction, the only remaining question is to whom and for how much.

Hi Folks, Over 3,500 items in the first week is great, but, a couple of notes: - Deleting items without buyer activity is bad form but it doesn't break the VFM. Tracking item location by page and number is unreliable. There is a less disruptive procedure for sellers to withdraw items explained on the admin page but after 10 years of asking sellers not to delete items, it still happens in every VFM. Clicking on the item time stamp (lower right of the item box) will put a link in your browser address bar that is always valid, regardless of shifts caused by item deletions. - Sellers deleting an item with a binding offer, that is an offer greater than or equal to the starting bid, equal to the BIN, or equal to the fixed price is a [b]SERIOUS violation[/b] of the terms of service. Buyers withdrawing binding offers is an equally serious violation of the ToS. If anyone has evidence of this happening, please report it directly to me.

I feel for you, I've had the same thing happen to me in the past. That's why this year, I've decided to just ignore the auction listings for now. A few weeks before the Con, if I'm still looking for a game on my wish list, I'll search and see if there are any auctions, but I'm hoping I can grab what I'm looking for with BINs and not have to be caught in limbo for 7-8 weeks.
I wish (I know it's probably a logistical headache so isn't realistic) that there could be a separate list for Auctions that doesn't open until say the first week of June and has a 2 week limit. That way people have time to find games that have BIN listings early on, and people are more inclined and excited to bid on auctions with a shorter time frame. I'm okay monitoring an auction for 2 weeks, especially if it's in its own section, not buried in the main list. The two week time frame also makes Auctions more of an event and I bet they would have more action if they were in their own list.
As it is, I'm loving all the BIN listings and have been able to pick up a lot of affordable copies of games for the kids to destroy or leave in their college common rooms, so I thank you all for that!

Are there rules around editing a minute detail of a post just for the subscription bump?

[q="tribefan07"]Are there rules around editing a minute detail of a post just for the subscription bump? [/q] The TOS includes this: "• [Sellers] Deleting an item followed by relisting (churning the list) to improve placement is strictly prohibited". While editing just for a subscription bump isn't expressly mentioned, it I suspect it go against the same "spirit" of this TOS item, namely "churning the list.", even if it is only "churning the subscription notices." It would be incredibly difficult to enforce though. For example, I have a note all my postings that I'm off to a sale this weekend and items may not be available over the weekend -- I have fantasies of removing that note on Monday. That isn't to bump anything, but your question made me realize it would. Is that bad? I think not, but figuring out someone's "intent" might be hard.

It's also a great idea to come prepared with envelopes with cash. I always put the buyers Real Name and User Name, item I purchased, and price on the envelope. Exact cash inside.
Usually as the buyer, you go and find the seller, but if you are going to be buying a lot and will have a wagon, it might be best to park yourself in a corner with a big sign with your name on it and ask if people wouldn't mind finding you as it's very chaotic the first 15-20 min. Also having a friend who can be a runner or cart watcher while you run is what a lot of people who both buy and sell. I know for me, I usually handle the selling side and my husband does the buy pickups and brings stuff back for me to hold.
The important thing is to have patience with everyone, we all find each other eventually!
Yeah I def thought of the envelope method - will def do so and glad that others have already done it before and find it useful!

I always send out a mass email to all my buyers and sellers that includes my contact info (and I ask to provide theirs as well), in case we need to make alternate arrangements, especially for the bigger games. I also always request cash in an envelope and I do the same and list the game, prices, and total amount in each envelope. That plus a spreadsheet listing all of this information, along with my wife helping out, makes it go a lot smoother and quicker than it would otherwise.

Three quick comments about the exchange scheduling:
- The exchange requires a lot of space and the early time is necessary to get that space and not to conflict with other scheduled events. Despite the size of this VFM, only about 10-15% of the attendees participate, and in the past some in the remaining 85-90% have been very vocal when the exchange intruded on gaming space, even if very briefly and at an odd hour.
- The exchange is always on day 2 of the convention, so always Thursday. People are still arriving at the venue on Wednesday, Friday and Saturday are the heaviest for gaming and DT events, and most people are packed and ready to leave on Sunday. Thursday also gives buyers plenty of opportunities to play their new treasures. We have always supported sellers making alternative arrangements as long as that requirement is clear in the item listing.
- The exchange is always 1 hour which will feel short and rushed to some. I have run 1, 1.5, and 2 hour exchanges and the result is always the same; 99.9% of the transactions are completed in the first hour and if the exchange runs longer, the rest of the time is spent waiting for that one person that feels entitled to show up in the last 5 minutes "to avoid the rush". With a 1 hour exchange there is no avoiding the rush, the brevity is a feature, not a bug.

Does anyone know what we can expect from Tom's Flea Market? Have not been before.

I missed last years, but assuming it didn't change, the general gist is he's offloading games that are being culled from the library or games that didn't make the cut. This doesn't mean there aren't good games. Don't get me wrong, we've gotten some stinkers from random pickups in the market, but we've also found some of our favorite games. It's a crap shoot but the prices are really good. It's a treasure hunt with good deals and most games, even crappy ones, are good for a single play through and then donate it, if it's not to your liking. My only exception was this sand game I picked up one year... that thing went in the garbage. I couldn't inflict it on someone else. It had literal sand in the box...
Anyway, the mechanism varies but each game has a color code dot with the price and the color price chart is everywhere. Once the line has gone through once, you can circle back through and whatever's left gets a mark down. The one time I made it to round three, instead of a further discount, it was grab a box and pay what you think it's worth. I usually tap out after two because I can't carry anymore, so I don't know if that happens every year.

Last year people who were very early in the line were allowed to get as many (or at least a large amount) of games as they wanted. I felt like I arrived fairly early to the line, but by the time I got into the room it had been picked clean by people who were first in line getting tons of games. Before most of us got into the room they announced that they put a limit on the number of purchases. I think it might have been 5 but I can't recal. You could then get back in line to go through again. Hopefully they implement the rule from the start this time. It was pretty dissapointing overall.

Tom's flea market is fun, but people will start lining up many hours before it opens, if I remember correctly. I have tended to find better deals more often in the VFM, but I think some of the games in Tom's flea market might have upgrades and painted minis. Also, as others have noted, pricing is done through color code dots, which are a nightmare if you are color blind. I understand why they do it, and given the difficulty of doing anything else they should probably keep doing it, but it would be nice if there were some other simple and easy system.
Oh! hopefully they take note and maybe use a number system instead of color (at least for the future).

[size=18][b]A note on high volume table assignments & late auctions.[/b][/size]
I know this information is coming a week too late, it will be communicated more clearly next year.
For various reasons the assignment of high volume tables is done at least a week before the convention. The selection criteria is by most total transactions, ie: items sold + items bought, these numbers can be obtained from either alpha tool. For DTE 2025 this selection was made last weekend (6/21) shortly before the map was published in the header.
Here is the catch; the alpha tools depend on either the BGG [u]Sold[/u] button and/or the keyword [b]sold[/b] to count a sale. The alpha tools do not recognize when an on-going auction has met the requirements for a pending sale. As a result, if you want your auctions to be counted as part of your transaction total, your auctions must end and the items must be properly marked as sold before that calculation is made, ie: roughly 1.5 weeks before the convention. Apologies to anyone with on-going auctions who would have set their end dates earlier to be included in the transaction count.
Please do not comment here, I will be more than happy to discuss this further in the [thread=3452199][b]VFM Admin Thread[/b][/thread]

I am a full-stack developer with a back-end focus by trade. For fun, I've been working on my own VFM tool, using an AWS Lambda backend and a RXJS Angular front-end, served out of S3. Oh and you have to be logged in to access the Geek Data page. All of those hoops just to get the few pieces of information that aren't present in the XMLAPI but should be readily available to their API developers, based on what is present in their API return. It's a glaring oversight.

Thanks for the advice and will take this over to the Geek Tools guild. Short version is I did read the TOS and the API auth token usage guidelines before I even started. My usage fits well within the guidelines. I did put together a POC to attempt the Geek Market scraping. It could be done in a manner that mimics a human, has minimum traffic, and you'd only need to do it once per sale, unless that scraping drifts from the output of the XMLAPI call to the Geek List (say in a canceled sale). Basically, it could be an eventual up-to-date process. However, after seeing the effort needed, I nixed that portion.
But I was more pointing out the hoops required to do the POC, when the data should be right there, given what else is already in the call. I have a theory on why those hoops exist and why it isn't present in the XMLAPI output already, but instead, I'll just add I hope your suggestion is incorporated. It's a good suggestion.

[b][size=18]Posting VFM Comments: How to/ToS/Policy/Tech Discussions, & Advertising[/size][/b] Hey everyone, congrats on making it this far, only one huge task remains in front of us. There are only 4 days of selling left so consider the following just to be guidance, next year these points will be incorporated into the ToS in one form or another.
Discussions about anything other than commerce (How to, ToS & Policies, BGG Tech, etc...) should be posted on the [thread=3452199][b]VFM Admin Thread[/b][/thread] Nearly anything related to the VFM can be discussed there and many of us long timers are subscribed and will respond. Please do not assist in policing content, if there's anything that needs to be addressed let me know by GeekMail or through the admin thread and I will handle it, most likely through a back-channel. We're hear to have fun and exchange some games, not worry too much about what gets posted where.
This is the first year we have allowed advertising in the VFM comments. In general I am a fan of how that has worked out. In my own case as an early poster it has helped to sell games late in the VFM and I also know I have purchased at least one game because an ad caught my attention. The ToS currently read "Promoting price reductions in the VFM comments section, including filtered links, is now permitted but please don't abuse this." but of course, one person's abuse is another's smart marketing. Next year the allowance will be specifically one personal post/week, maybe two in the wind-down period after the exchange instructions have been posted.
If anyone has comments on this post, please do so on the [thread=3452199][b]VFM Admin Thread[/b][/thread] where I would be happy to continue the conversation.

The sellers in the non-high volume room seems very chaotic if I'm understanding correctly. Are there no assigned tables in this room? It seems like it was much more organized last year, but I was in the high volume room last year so I'm not sure. I'm probably posting this too late for it to matter though.

[q="agentkuo"]The sellers in the non-high volume room seems very chaotic if I'm understanding correctly. Are there no assigned tables in this room? It seems like it was much more organized last year, but I was in the high volume room last year so I'm not sure. I'm probably posting this too late for it to matter though.[/q] It is similar to last year except the two room are together. The free exchange has always been chaotic although it has become less so with more than half of all transactions taking place in the high volume room.

Someone accidentally left a copy of Harry Potter Hogwarts Battle at our table. We are in the high volume area.
Edit: Found the owner!

It took me as long to do 8 transactions this year as it did 50 in previous years because of the limiting of people going in. Keeping sellers outside does not make sense. Keeping buyers outside does not make sense. We ended up with 95% of people inside together at the end, anyway.

Bob please pass along our thanks to the crew and volunteers that helped with the event. Everyone seemed excited and happy to pick up their new games!
Overall I think it's a great event and the high volume side went smoothly. My suggestions for tweaks for next year would be in the non-high volume area that we have alphabetical sections. Just having a A-F corner, G-M corner, etc would have made it easier to direct buyers what section of the room someone would be in. My other suggestion would be that if we're to have it at 8am next year, please let us do it in the Open Gaming area because it's so much bigger. Only a few people game that early and we could leave a few tables on one side reserved for gaming. When we were finished about 0915, we walked past the open gaming and it was almost deserted. There wouldn't have been a need to hold people in the hallway until 0830 if we had been in the larger space. I think giving buyers a direction to go to find their sellers and allowing everyone in at the start would have allowed everyone to more quickly retrieve their items.

For those sending messages to High Volume sellers who HAD TABLES that you couldn't find us, you didn't look very hard.
I'm sorry but there is a photo of where the high volume sellers were. My wife and I wore a neon green shirts with my name on it. I wasn't hard to find.
I'm making this post in regard to all the high volume sellers who stood there wondering where the ppl who bought our stuff were. There is a picture at the top of this page.

Agreed on alphabetized sections, Cali. I believe the size and the organization this year is up to the DT Crew, though. I think having a general alphabetized section as we've had I the past would help.
I think the size of the space would have been fine if everyone was let In at the start, but a larger area for the event would make it go a lot faster, too.

[size=18]An [article=46292349][b]After-action Report[/b][/article] has been posted on the VFM Admin Thread.[/size] I am happy to discuss feedback, it is all considered and helps. I am going to post all follow up on the [thread=3452199][b]VFM Admin Thread[/b][/thread]. Even though this comment section is now unmoderated, the two-lines-at-a-time format isn't optimal for a conversation.
Unrelated, [b]did anyone get a picture of the Exchange?[/b] I always take one but forgot this year. If anyone has a high angle shot, I would appreciate a copy at bob@bobgallosolutions.com. Thanks.

I ended up being the 4th highest buyer (I think) and had 15 sales with 45 buys roughly to do for the event. I had to do a transaction a minute to fit in an hour, but could not get into the room until nearly 8:35 after showing up at 7:45. I did not leave the event space until close to 9:40 as the last in the hall. Several people I was supposed to meet had left as they thought I wouldn't show as I was in the high traffic area awhile. I had everything in envelopes to do transactions quickly, but the hall was not organized well, even the high traffic area compared to last year. I actually had more transactions to do than several of the high volume area sellers, but the decisions in that regard, layout, and entry timings made it a more cumbersome event than it should have been.
Maybe add an express line or 10m early entry for some of the highest number of transactions outside high volume sellers? Especially for high buy transaction numbers. A more linear table layout to snake through would also help (like last year).
I sold 15, bought twice that amount and I thought the event was great. Thanks, Bob. ^^b

@[username=viperfang4][/username] I think many of your concerns are addressed in the [article=46292349][b]after-action report[/b][/article] and if not, I would be happy to discuss there... however... there is one point that everyone still reading this list should see and we will be stressing again next year:
Participating in the VFM requires agreeing to either a [u][b]full[/b][/u], one hour commitment to the Exchange (regardless of the number of transactions) or making alternative arrangements [u][b]before[/b][/u] the con. Leaving the exchange early with unfinished business is rude to your transaction partners and against the ToS.

Sellers: The BGG commission invoice that was issued Aug 3 is the invoice that must be paid if you have not done so already. Please remember the commission fee is not optional and is not charged by DT admin, this is a fee paid to BGG for the use of their platform for commercial purposes.

item.comment: For Ankh is there any negotiation room? Or possible trade with some money?

A trade would be difficult, I am looking to clear space. As for negotiating, it's early... I'm inclined to let this one stand at this price for a few weeks. If it's still available in June I'll get back to you and if you're still interested, maybe we can work something out.
Sounds good. I will keep an eye out.
Let me know. If you may be interested in a trade plus some cash?

Hi Ryan, sorry for the delay. I am trying to lower my game count and I've been pretty good at buying very little, SETI is the only base game purchase I made this go-around. I would like to pickup Undaunted 2200: Callisto, and the new versions of Nexus Ops & Ethnos but I don't really see them being a part of a trade even with additional cash.
Sorry I have a signed copy of Song of fire and ice that I picked up through the jack vasel auction that haven't played. I was told by my wife get ride of something before you get anymore.

And checking. does this qualify for the BOGO? Didn't know if this one was specially marked, or if that was earlier verbiage and all of your listings now qualified?

This does not qualify for the BOGO1/2 (applied to games over $150), but it does have a $10 purchase credit which would be just as good or better on an item $20 or less (note: purchase credits don't stack, the largest applies). If you are looking at something over $20, let me know and depending on the item I might be able to cut a deal.
All purchase $10 or over also qualify for a free item from [url=https://boardgamegeek.com/geeklist/352224/2025-dice-tower-east-virtual-flea-market?itemid=11872497#11872497][b]here[/b][/url]. One free item per person.
Let's BOGO this and Star Trek Ascendancy please :)

Hey Ben, I screwed up and my first response was incorrect, but I will honor the BOGO. I am going to split the discount between the listings to not skew BGG statistics too much. $65 + ($65*0.5) = $97.50 total which I will mark as $48.75 each.

item.comment: Hi. I was hoping to get some clarification. Was this first edition from the Kickstarter? If so, was it the Standard, Deluxe, or Legendary edition? Thank you!

(Mike) All First Edition copies were from the same initial print run as the Kickstarter rewards. Which of the 3 editions this copy is will be printed on the back cover of the box. Note that all First Editions included the Oracle tile and had the Shapeshifter miniature and standee hidden beneath the bottom tray. (I am sure there are still undiscovered shapeshifters out there!)
Hello! I believe standard, I purchased this the day it hit my FLGS. I bought it, sleeved it and its been on the shelf ever since! Just too busy for me!

Thank you for your response (and very cool to see the creator/publisher dropping in here). If it's only the standard edition, I can offer $60. If it's either of the other two versions, I would definitely increase my offer. Thank you!
(Mike) So many games! I love seeing games find good homes. Enjoy all your play!
Just took another look at mine, has two of the larger miniatures in the bottom tray and the two empty boxes for the deluxe edition and mini bases!

(Mike) I am guessing the back of the box says "2nd Edition". Second Edition copies of Dwellings of Eldervale come with the Frost Giant and Mother of Dragons (optional game play). This means your copy will not have the Oracle tile or Shapeshifter mercenary as they are separate purchases now.
So, just so I'm sure what I'm bidding on, this doesn't include what one would get in the deluxe or Legendary upgrade packs? Thanks (again) for your help!
Well I was mistaken! If I actually looked at the box...2nd Standard Edition
Thanks for figuring it out. I'm still willing to offer $60, but understand if you're holding out. Thank you!

I'll probably wait to see if any of the fancier copies pop up first (the problem is I played the game once and loved it, so I know I'm going to end up getting the deluxe and/or legendary upgrades anyway, which aren't cheap). Anyway, if nothing pops up over the next month or so, I may check in closer to the con to see if this is still available. Thank you, though.

[size=9][url=https://www.yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/352224?Seller=ukla%20the%20mock&Status=NotSold]Click here to view all my items available for sale[/url][/size]

No, not really. I do right now because it makes it easier to list here. The link I added to my comment shows all of what I have up on this list.

You have a great collection. We love the same games. I am jealous of your Andromeda's Edge. Are you over The Great Zimbabwe? I'd give you our Civ games and 30 Extra dollars for that one. You don't have Senoire, do you? I didn't see it with Nippon or Madera.

I think I'm gonna pass on the Zimbabwe trade. The player in me still wants it. Only the collector in me really wants this. Thanks for hashing it out with me, though. I appreciate you.

item.comment: I'm interested. I am new to the game community and first time Dice tower attendee. How does it work to claim this game?

Welcome. To buy a game usually a person would comment with "BIN" (buy it now at listed price) or something like "I'll buy it for $10". To make an offer lower than the asking price say something like "I'd offer $7". The seller can ignore you, agree to your offer or counter-offer. If the offer is accepted, the seller will mark it as sold. You will receive a geekmail from BGG confirming your purchase and asking you to give feedback on the seller. (You can do this after the convention.) Then on Thursday morning at the convention we will meet at the designated location to complete the purchase. Unless otherwise agreed upon, it will be a cash purchase.
I'll mark it sold once you comment back.

item.comment: Sorry Mark, this is not a auction. The price is fixed.
Ok, no problem. You may want to post that as this is a virtual auction.

Mark, its more a mix between geek market style list listings and auctions, it's why it is called the "Virtual Flea Market". The organizer did encourage people to us FP or fixed price instead of BIN if it is a fixed price listing, but BIN is such a common bit of vernacular that you can assume a listing is fixed price if it only lists a BIN and doesn't list an end date.
Whatever you say but I have bought and sold on this VFM for several years and have bid on just BINs before. The suggestion was for the benefit of those, like me, who would possibly purchase from you.

Yah making offers on BIN only listings is super common on here, and maybe I shouldn't have chimed in since it isn't my listing. I was also just trying to chime in and offer helpful clarification, but my assumption with part of Chrys's saying it is not an auction is that he didn't want you to think that the $15 was a binding price, where you had won the item, since you worded it as a bid and not an offer.
Will, I get that. Nice way to clarify. I would not personally see my bid as binding. If the selling says it’s not enough, I accept that.

The TOS was updated recently clarifying the point
[q]An item with a BIN but no starting bid and no end time is not an auction and is functionally the same as a fixed price offer.[/q]
The TOS refers to what you did as an "offer" which is non-binding rather than a "bid" which is a binding agreement as part of an auction.

item.comment: Hey Warren, don't think I've asked you this yet ... any interest in trades? about 1/2 my stuff is already posted, but you could find the remaining list at http://d3x.net/CurrentGamesForSale.html in the meantime.
If Ken C doesn't get it, I'll BIN. Thanks

At this point the bedroom that serves as Sharon's and my game library is stuffed to the gills - we're talking Monty Python "wafer-thin mint" territory. So I'm afraid I'm in cull mode as opposed to trade mode.

pass it on to Sean ... I'd love to get it, but the shelf of shame is almost 100 games at the moment and I'm trying SO hard not to pick up too many. Sean ... if you're up for it, my wife (I'll claim she is, at least) and I would love to play this with you once after you pick it up.
@Ken C - For sure! Would love to get this game in at the con.
@Famazar - do you want to BIN for $20? You mentioned that in an earlier message but wanted to confirm after the later message traffic.
Sold! See you at the exchange.

item.comment: It has DV1-022 on the side, so I suppose that's the 2022 edition?

[q="Farsol"]It has DV1-022 on the side, so I suppose that's the 2022 edition?[/q]
That's just it's stock number. The 2nd Edition has "2nd Edition" printed on the box and on the rulebook cover. The general consensus is that 2nd Ed is completely unplayable hot garbage. I know that 3rd edition is printed on the rulebook cover. I assume it's also on the box? Not sure. I own 1st edition, which of course doesn't have any "edition" on the box or rulebook. DVG did release an upgrade kit for 1st and 2nd to 3rd Ed, giving a new board, rulebook, and more. It's $9.99 direct from DVG. Shipping is $16.65 to FL. Which is why my copy is headed for the wood chipper; I'm tired of it taking up space. 🤬
I confirmed that this is the First Edition from 2015. No markings of later editions on any of the box or cover pages.

item.comment: Hi would you do this and underwater cities for $50?

Hi Russell, I think you might have missed this comment as I saw you just sold Underwater Cities for $25 - which would have been essentially this at asking + Underwater Cities for $25. I was more interested in Underwater Cities so this offer was contingent on both, let me know if my offer could still be accepted since I had commented first. Apologies on not commenting on both listings to avoid confusion.

You are right. I didn't see the comment on Evacuation and then, seeing the offer on Underwater Cities, I took that offer.
I know that the offer you made has prices equivalent to the offer I ultimately accepted and yours came first, however I didn't see an offer on UC at the time I accepted... and I publicly committed the sale to the other party on the VFM and I feel bound to honor that sale.
I am sorry for my part in the confusion. As a consolation, I would be happy to sell you Evacuation for $20. I recognize that you wanted Underwater Cities more, but it's the best I feel I can do in this circumstance.
$20 for Evacuation is fine with me! Thank you.

I would have bought it for $8 but congrats Paul.
I believe the counter offer should have been to Adrian since it was still listed for $10.

[q="NocturnalAllen"]I believe the counter offer should have been to Adrian since it was still listed for $10.[/q] I don't think so, at least according to the ToS in the Admin thread: "It is acceptable to offer less than the Fixed Price or Starting Bid (a "low ball" offer), however, such an offer is non-binding on either party. It is up to the seller to decide how to respond to a low ball offer and they are not obligated to respond at all. Low ball offers are non-binding until both parties have confirmed agreement to the offer."
IMHO, that's the risk you take when you make a low ball offer.

This was not someone taking the BIN price after someone else low-balled. This was a counter-offer to a specific person. The original price was $10, as it still shows, ironically.
Adrian, if you see this, I'll give you my copy of Point City. Actually, I'll message you, as well.

item.comment: If this is already opened & everything verified complete, no moldy box, etc. I will BIN for $10.
No moldy box? what do you mean?

Last year had a bad run of NIS boxes with mold in the box! Usually means factory problem or forgot to pack a dessicant inside. So one more reason to be paranoid about unopened (on top of unopened KS games that might have broken/missing/duplicate components) 🙂
If a game is NIS, how would anyone know it had mold? or missing pieces?

They wouldn’t. Two of the moldy boxes I ran into were NIS from OLGS, and I bought a KS game unpunched (but also not inventoried) secondhand .. it was missing some of the plastic bits. Fun when you unbox and inventory.
Rare for crowdfunding, even more for non- crowdfunded, but happens.
Anyway, looking forward to playing this one!

I haven't eyeballed it in a while since I have like 2,000 to sell, but I'll hit you up close to the con when I pack if I see anything noteworthy. It's buried in the back room but shrink was removed so I'll be able to check.
I’m sure it’ll be fine. 2000? yikes!
I skipped BGG and BGG Spring, so I have lots piled up.

[q="BradleySugarman"]$75?[/q]
Based on the current geek market, this price is very generous.
Fair enough. I saw one sell last week on ebay for $80. If you change your mind let me know.

I don't go based on "a copy sold for xyz." I don't know the condition of that game or the desperation of that seller to get rid of the game plus on Ebay you can stack the shipping category in order to have a lower "sell" price so you don't owe Ebay as much.
Plus with supply and demand, I look at current listings, not old listings.

item.body:
[size=24][b]HUGE PILE OF MAGE KNIGHT STUFF![/b][/size]
[b][i]How much stuff is there?[/i][/b] Lots!
[i][b]How many pre-painted miniatures? [/b][/i]I don't know---hundreds.
[b][i]How many hundreds? [/i][/b]I don't know. At LEAST one hundred, probably two, maybe more.
[b][i]What kind of stuff? [/i][/b]The miniatures and terrain/castle stuff. A LOT of unopened, new-in-box stuff, including a whole case of unopened Minions Boosters.
[b][i]Are there any dragons?[/i][/b] Yes.
[b][i]Do you have pictures?[/i][/b] Yes. I'll post as many as I can so you can get an overview.
[i][b]Would I get a poster? [/b][/i]There is a poster, yes. You can have it.
[b][i]What can I do with all this Mage Knight Stuff? [/i][/b]Well, you could play it. Or you could use the miniatures for your RPG campaigns. Or you could blow stuff up with firecrackers.
[b][i]Can I just buy certain pieces instead of the whole lot? [/i][/b]No, I'd rather not do that. Just take everything, please.
[b][i]How much?[/i][/b] Let's try an auction with a very low starting bid.
[b][size=18]AUCTION [Ends June 20 at 11:59pm Eastern][/size][/b]
[b][size=18]Starting Bid: $25
Bid Increments: $5
BIN: $220
Cash, Venmo or Cash App[/size][/b]
[imageid=8919316 medium]
item.comment: These are the piles that make me weak. $30 :)

I used to play in the sanctioned tournaments at cons and collect the promos but have long since divested myself of it. They lost me at MK 2.0. Feels good to see a nice pile of this stuff still around!

I'll BIN for $220. Thank you for this mountain of goodness! On the off chance you have other such mountains of other long-dead minis games please let me know. Love Mech Warriors, AT-43, Confrontation, etc. Cheers!
If this had been MW, I would have BINed right away. Didn't really need MK. The pile does kinda look like my HeroClix collection. LoL
I'll take a look! I'm sure I have some other minis games I'd be happy to part with.

I have lots of Mage Knight Dungeons minis I got for homebrew dungeon crawler. Great stuff. Forgot I had one of those MK dragons. The AT-43 apes are great, I use them for Gorilla Grod minions :) So I'd also be curious what other stuff is in the vault :)

[size=9][url=https://www.yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/352224?Seller=kshelto1&Status=NotSold]Click here to view all my items available for sale[/url][/size]
item.comment: This is tempting, as I would love to have the money and cards. When people ask me "what was your first game that got you into the hobby?"...my answer is always "Acquire"...same box, same money, same cards. I still have that game, but the money is so curled, lol! It received much play in the 1970's! But I like my board better, and I would not be buying it for the collection value...only refreshed money and cards. If you wanted to sell it for $20, I would take it...but I totally understand the collector value. Hope you find that person.

These are hard to part with due to the memories for me as well. My father and I meant to play the war games together but sadly we never got the chance. I am going to keep the price. I'll keep them if nothing else. Thanks.
I assume it's not worth $20 to get it off your shelf...? Just want to check it off my list so as not to keep checking on it.

I too own 2 versions already, AH '99 BB and an old 3M but with plastic tiles. If you are taking offers and it is complete (inventoried?) I'd offer $25 (then I'd probably unload my other 3M plastic tile version)
Everything has been inventoried and is present. It's in virtually unplayed condition so I am pretty firm on the price.
Hope you find the right new owner. I think I will finally open that new copy I have sitting on the shelf and see how it feels 🙂

item.body:
Ogre Designer's Edition + Tote carry bag and a ton of Promos, etc... I bought the game sealed from a local store with the box damage as shown below. Then pieced together everything else over the next couple years.
[imageid=8937069]
NOTE: Only missing the kickstarter "Overlays" and "Vulcan" counter sheets (2 of each). [b][u]ALL [/u][/b]other sheets from the original release are included. Some twice!
SB $200 BIN $250
NOTE: Base box came with 32 counter sheets. All are punched/assembled and organized in the box (I never got around to gluing the 3D Ogres so some are a bit wobbly) + Custom, laminated counter dividers + Laminated, individual Ogre battle tracking sheets & dry erase pens
+ Kickstarter exclusive counter sheets (only 2 of the 6 sheets): (K1/K2) Targets go Boom = 2 sheets (punched / assembled in the box)
+ Sponsored/Promo sheets: (punched / assembled in the box) (A6 *2) Nihon Empire: North American Divisions = 4 sheets (2 each copy) (M3/M4) BGG Exclusive Overlays = 2 sheets (N1) BGG 3D Units = 2 sheets (1st copy)
+ Sponsored/Promo sheets: (sealed) (B5/K2/L2) Ogre: Nightfall = 3 sheets (E5/E6) Uncommon Ogres = 4 sheets (2 each copy) (N1) BGG 3D Units = 2 sheets (2nd copy) (O1) Strategic and Tactical Objectives = 1 sheet (R1) ACD Distribution Sponsored Sheet = 1 sheet (B3/B4) Barbarians At the Gate = 4 sheets (2 each copy) + 1 booklet "Barbarians At the Gate" Supplement from Scalpel Games
+ Ogre Objective 218 (expansion - Sealed) + Ogre Pocket edition (where it all began! - Sealed)
+ Burned Mini-CD with 31 MB of Ogre related spreadsheets and pdf's

See this thread: https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1662840/article/38997037#38997037
I thought there was a KSE for Bruce but not finding on original campaign, so maybe I was thinking Unmatched or Dragon Tides not another GBG game.

[q="dontnickme"]Just for my own collection sake, all the Yashima items I know are Base, Deep Woods, Icy Peaks, Legends of Fairy Tales (chinese historical?), Wizard Promo, Promo pack which has Alt Art and Level Up cards.[/q]
Same. My copy is currently…
Retail Base game with - Icy Peaks, Deep Woods & Fairytale expansions - Token packs: Frost/Trap & Seed/Plant/Fire - Promo Pack #1 ---- Level-Up Pack (+3 cards for 11 kami masters, all but Bruce Lee) ---- Alternate Art Pack (base game alt art)
…and if I win also the Wizard promo!
Oh the token packs I forgot I dont have, but I'm fine with that. I care more about cards and minis heh. LMK if you ever see a cheap token pack tho!

[q="dontnickme"]Oh the token packs I forgot I dont have, but I'm fine with that. I care more about cards and minis heh. LMK if you ever see a cheap token pack tho![/q] After many years of searching I found one on ebay from a store I was getting something else from.

We rate on a 6-pt scale (like Heavy Cardboard or the Hidden Gems Boardgame Podcast) -- for me this might be a '5', for her it was more of a high '3'. Since it is 2p only, and she's my primary 2p partner, that means it goes away. This is a serious headgame ... what are they going to do? How much do I offer? What can I get away with? Tray #1: Be Not Afraid Cursed!

item.comment:
I love this game, and want to see more people enjoy it!
I will include a set of 2 3D printed goals for FREE to the winner of this item!
[imageid=8867161]
I'm interested, but what does fp stand for?
[q="Elium"]I'm interested, but what does fp stand for?[/q] Fixed Price

Fixed Price of $150. BJ, Thanks for that generous offer a set of 2 3D printed goals for FREE to the winner of this item! I love hockey and this game looked like fun, but my wife was not interested in it, so I want to find it a good home. It has never been played yet. The miniatures look awesome! Joshua, if you are still interested let me know.
I'm afraid that's a bit to rich for my blood, atm. I followed both Kickstarters. It looks great!
Joshua, what are you willing to offer for it? I will consider your offer if it is fair.

Feel free to tell me to pound sand, but I can offer $50 for this. My justification is my *need* to get the 1st Edition Update pack for this, and shipping, customs, etc is not cheap from the publisher.
Can we meet in the middle at $75? Still a great deal!

[q="BarbnCarl"]Can we meet in the middle at $75? Still a great deal![/q] Nah, sorry, I really can't. Not trying to haggle you so badly, I can justify it at $100 (after paying $50 for the update pack) but not any more. It's similar to you, the theme has me on board, but it won't be something my wife is going to be super into.
I will sell it to you for $50, if you are still interested

[q="BarbnCarl"]I will sell it to you for $50, if you are still interested[/q]
Awesome, thanks!!

[-] [B]BIN: [/B] $15 (firm, it is what I paid for it ... yes, I know it is currently $22 on Amazon; that makes this a bit more than a 25% discount ... but it is essentially new, in great shape, and mostly sealed). [B]Condition: [/B] Only the starting scenario is opened, the rest of the game is still sealed
We played this last night and I enjoyed it, but it isn't optimized for 2p only which is where much of my gaming is (particularly for co-ops) and I'm super tight on shelf space. Once we finish both versions of The Crew, I suspect we'll come back to this -- the artwork is super cool and I like the way that they manage "missions" through character objectives.

Played this last night (the 18th). Much better than I expected, but not as good as it needed to be to displace something from my very tight shelves. A mix of action selection and worker placement. I suspect this is better at lower player counts (we played with 2) than with the highest (4p) -- I think it would get to be more of an experience and less of a strategic or tactical game there. But, for 2p or 3p, this isn't a bad gateway game at all.

the other way is to simply go through my for trade list....
https://boardgamegeek.com/collection/user/JeffyJeff?trade=1&subtype=boardgame&ff=1
you can click on "geek rating" to have BGG sort (click again to reverse sort) by geek rating.

As an incentive to buy [url=https://www.yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/352224?Seller=kaelius&Status=NotSold]more of my games[/url], I'll add in the following ... I've been cleaning out my workspace and have some electronics I need to get rid of. I don't feel like I can drop game prices as others have, but buy games and I'll toss them in as perks -- [i]I'm selling the games, not the electronics -- these are just incentives to buy the games[/i].
The laptops all have issues -- see the notes. But even if you just choose to strip them for parts to sell on ebay, it's probably a win. I just don't have time for it right now. I was using most of the phones as cameras for my Octoprint setups (3D printing) before switching to raspberry pi clones and real webcams. All systems (phones or laptops) have been freshly reset/wiped and I ran sdelete on the laptops to wipe free space. All phones were used originally on either Verizon or Visible. I believe all are unlocked (unless otherwise noted) but I don't know how to verify this with certainty. These are all added/perked in "as-is".
[b]For a purchase of ...[/b] [b]any game -- (tablet) Google Nexus 7" tablet[/b]. Has a broken screen with a dead area ... by rotating you can get to everything, but it's annoying. It was working fine, but is now stuck -- the issue is that I did a fresh install/reset on it and it is now at a screen prompting to join a network. The "skip" button is greyed out. It can SEE networks, but can't join any. I don't know what's going on with it.
[b]$5 -- (laptop) Lenovo Ideapad s405[/b]. AMD A6 4455m, 2.1Ghz, 2-core, 4GB, win 10 home. Has case damage and lid trouble -- missing hinge covers and back corner isn't secure. Something is wrong with it ... like the tablet above, it can see networks, but can't join any. I haven't tried the ethernet cable. Didn't test the battery but expect it is terrible.
[b]$10 -- (phone) Samsung Galaxy J36V[/b], boots with a Verizon screen so probably locked to Verizon. Held a charge ~1 hr (with screen off).
[b]$20 -- (phone) I believe this is an Essential PH-1?[/b] Freshly "reset", but running OctaviOS. Unlocked but shows as "corrupt" when it boots since the kernel wasn't properly signed, I think -- it has been a good while since I loaded this kernel on it. Regardless, once you press the power button to bypass the "hey, something's wrong!" screen, it works fine, although it may be a wifi only device from now on. Screen is cracked (badly) but responsive. In 'setup' shows as a "Phh Trebel with GApps". 128GB storage. I don't know how long the battery will last, but it has been up for about 17 hours at this point.
[b]$30 -- (phone) Google Pixel 2 XL.[/b] It had a bad battery which expanded and in replacing it (or as part of it expanding), the screen was damaged -- no cracks, but the entire left half "fuzzes" or looks like there's an equalizer coming out of the left edge. Screen is responsive though, even in the wonky area. Since battery was recently replaced, battery life is good. It has been up with the clock showing for over 16 hours at this point and shows 77% battery remaining.
[b]$30 -- (phone) Google Pixel 3A[/b]. Upper right of the screen and case is cracked, but it doesn't seem to affect functionality at all. Has been up for about 10 hours and shows 87% battery remaining.
[b]$35 -- (laptop) Toshiba Satellite C55-C.[/b] Intel Pentium N3700 1.6Ghz 4-core, 8GB. CD drive, 460GB HD. Win 10 home finishing updating. Major crack in case near where the power cord goes in -- I had to use a toothpick to stick inside the case to hold the power cord acceptor in place when plugging it in, but otherwise seems to be in good shape. No battery test yet.
[b]$40 -- (laptop) ASUS UX303U. Touchscreen.[/b] i5-6200 @2.3Ghz, 2-core, 8GB. Good bit of case damage, lid won't stay up at the right angle (it droops) and there's an obvious gap in the case when you try to close it. Running Win 10 home fully updated/patched as of 6/19/2025. Other than the case, seems to run/work fine. Disabled power saving, left screen on, used windows clock/stopwatch and it has been up for 4hr48min and suggests 2hr51min 36% battery remaining.
Feel free to ask questions here or in geekmail.

Embark on an exhilarating journey like never before! Equipped with cutting-edge technology and a state-of-the-art diving submarine, you stand at the precipice of a legendary discovery: the enigmatic Atlantis.
Finding Atlantis is a competitive deduction and exploration game with unique app-generated puzzles for 1-4 players. On a turn, you play two cards from your hand and resolve the action on these cards, moving your submarines on the map; inspecting the ocean floor via periscope, sonar, and radiograph; exploring for artifacts or stealing those artifacts from opponents; dropping mines to slow down those opponents; and surfacing to reset your deck. You track your findings on a hidden map, trying to be the first to discover all spaces of Atlantis.
Finding Atlantis features an app that offers more than a million distinct and challenging sea maps, along with an integrated tutorial and a U-Bot mode that allows for solo play against an AI or AI-controlled opponents that can be added to a multiplayer game. -BoardGameGeek.com

Imperial Settlers: Roll & Write is a standalone game set in the universe of Imperial Settlers and Imperial Settlers: Empires of the North. The game is heavily focused on engine building! Constructing buildings grants you a special bonus, and with each passing turn the game offers you more choices as your empire gains momentum. Imperial Settlers: Roll & Write has two game modes. The standard mode is a 2-4 player competitive challenge in which you try to gain more points than your opponents. The adventure mode for a single player offers 48 unique game sheets. Each sheet presents unique challenges and gameplay as players have different buildings at the start. Tweak your engine and get as many points as you can! Grab your pencil, roll your dice, and create the most prosperous empire! -BoardGameGeek.com
